{"decision":"Anthony, 2026-08-17, looking ahead to a future increment doing proper SE on reflow2 itself: 'we talked about 8 subsystems of reflow2, but currently there were not really any black-boxes... when we do this SE task, this SPECIFIES edge will be needed between each black-box.'

THE DIRECTION IS RIGHT AND THE MECHANISM NEEDS ONE CORRECTION, recorded so the future increment does not start by drawing the wrong edges. SPECIFIES does not run BETWEEN two black boxes. It runs from a machine-readable contract ARTIFACT to the INTERFACE that sits between them. Three distinct edges are needed and they answer three different questions:

  PROVIDES / CONSUMES   Component -> Interface   WHO offers this boundary, and who needs it. This is the edge between black boxes, and it is what is missing today (`fact:the-eight-subsystems-are-groupings-not-black-boxes`: 0 of 8 subsystems provide anything).
  SPECIFIES             Artifact  -> Interface   WHICH FILE is the authoritative contract. This is what makes the boundary CHECKABLE instead of prose, and it is the edge that has never been drawn anywhere in the graph.
  REALIZES              Artifact  -> Component   which code implements the box. Already drawn everywhere.

So the SE increment owes, per boundary: an Interface node, a PROVIDES and one or more CONSUMES, and a SPECIFIES to whatever file actually defines the contract. Drawing SPECIFIES alone between subsystems that provide nothing would attach contracts to boundaries that do not exist.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. `req:interface-spec-complete` says a published interface must carry enough to check compatibility rather than prose; `seam_report` and `granularity_report` read the interface tier. With 0 of 8 subsystems providing anything, those computations have nothing to read above the leaves — the decomposition is invisible to every tool that reasons about seams.","name":"A black box is defined by PROVIDES/CONSUMES; SPECIFIES is what makes its contract checkable rather than prose","rationale":"HIS STANDING GROUND, stated in the same breath and applying to the whole of this: 'I'm more interested in doing things right. If that requires redoing work, so be it - I prefer quality. So if adding SPECIFIES is right, then we have our answer regardless of the amount of work that it includes.' That closes the cost objection in advance for the SE increment, which will be a large one — the boundaries have to be designed, not merely recorded.

A COUPLING THE SEQUENCING MUST RESPECT, found while answering this. Adding subsystem interfaces adds PROVIDES/CONSUMES edges, which ARE traversed by propagation (Lateral, both directions). Making SPECIFIES propagate would add more. Both ENLARGE every blast radius and therefore every scoped region — at exactly the moment `dec:the-default-scope-depth-should-be-two` is shrinking depth to make regions mean something. The two pull against each other, so the depth change should land and be re-measured BEFORE the SE work adds edges, and re-measured again after. Otherwise a region that got usable will quietly stop being so and nothing will say which change did it.

WHY THE SE INCREMENT IS NOT CREATED HERE: he said 'in some future increment', which is a statement of intent rather than a schedule. Capturing it without scheduling it is the honest half.","status":"proposed"}
